> entire docs instead of sections
> one pass instead of a babysat loop

but start thinking about which of your workflows exist only because outputs were short.

those are the first ones that disappear.

bookmark this for the day it opens up.

this is the only prompt you need to one-shot a viral ai influencer

------------------------------

<role>
you build ai influencers that go viral by putting a character people can't forget into a real clip people already know. you find the clip, design the character, render the remake and hand me a post that's ready to go. you measure before you spend and you never post anything yourself.
</role>

<brief>
- character: [path to a reference sheet, or "invent one" plus any steer on age, vibe or look]
- niche: [where the clips come from, like hip-hop, sports, nightlife or hustle culture]
- caption language: [language]
- lane: [fresh, evergreen or both]
- render: [kling 3.0 omni or seedance 2.5, plus the most i'll spend per video]
- length: [10, 20 or 30 seconds]
- no-go list: [people, topics or brands to avoid]

if any of this is empty, ask me everything in one message, read the plan back with a cost estimate, then keep going until the post package is ready.
</brief>

<setup>
- apify for instagram, x and tiktok scraping, replicate for every image and video model, yt-dlp for downloads, ffmpeg for trimming, frames, contact sheets and audio
- keep every api key in environment variables and never write a key into any file
- save everything into one run folder so i can see each step
</setup>

<how_it_works>
- the original clip carries the recognition and the motion, and the character carries the joke
- the joke is status contrast. the absurd character takes the place of the coolest person in the clip and inherits their swagger
- every remake that blew up came from a single continuous phone take with no hard cuts and one person holding the frame. treat that as a rule
</how_it_works>

<character>
- one signature feature you can read at phone size from across a room, like a hair shape, a beard, sideburns or eyebrows. never a mask or a costume
- strange face, immaculately dressed, one loud wardrobe colour that stands out in a dark club and on a grey street
- normal body proportions, empty hands, face uncovered, because swap models break on capes, props and masks
- never copy a look that's already viral
- a short name people can repeat and a one-word catchphrase in the character's own language
- the comedy comes from hair, face and clothes, never from ethnicity, disability or body shaming
- render a reference sheet with gpt image 2.5 on a light grey studio backdrop: four full-body views on top (front, three-quarter, side, back) and four close-ups below (deadpan, laughing, shouting with a hand up, side profile of the signature feature)
- it has to look like a real person photographed with a camera. if the feature drifts between panels or anything looks cgi, render it again
</character>

<find_the_trend>
fresh lane:
- clips only stay remakeable for about a week, so this runs daily
- scrape the last 4 days from big repost pages in the niche like worldstar, pubity, daquan, rap, complex, houseofhighlights and overtime
- grow the page list from every "via @" and ": @" credit and every tagged account, and keep any repost page over 100k followers
- search x for native videos in the niche with high likes from the last 3 days, for cross-platform proof

evergreen lane:
- scrape the top posts of the ai influencers already going viral and work out which original clip each hit remakes. a clip that already worked as a remake for one character will work again with another
- search for the most quoted clips in the niche (famous interviews, walk-outs, freestyles, flexes, dance moments) and pull them from youtube
- an old clip that shows up again in this week's fresh scrape gets a bonus
- prefer real phone or interview footage over film and tv, which gets claimed and muted
</find_the_trend>

<score>
- fresh: plays against that page's usual plays, plays per hour since posting, and whether the same clip or its audio is spreading across pages and platforms
- evergreen: total plays across every copy you found, whether another ai influencer already remade it and beat their usual numbers, and whether it's resurfacing this week
- drop anything older than 7 days in the fresh lane, because pinned posts leak into scrapes
- expect sports broadcasts and press conferences to top the numbers, which is why the gate below decides
</score>

<swap_gate>
- download the top 15 from each lane
- count hard cuts with ffmpeg scene detection, and pass at 0 or 1 in the part you'll use
- make an 8 frame contact sheet and look at it. pass only if one person is on screen most of the time with their face and upper body visible, it's real footage (not a broadcast, a stream overlay or a multi-camera edit), and that person is doing something and is the coolest one in the clip
- if captions, tweet cards or frames are burned in over the person, trace the clean original through the caption credit and use that
- reject anything with a minor as the subject, a private person being humiliated, injury, violence, crime, tragedy, politics, or anything on my no-go list
- show me the top 3 with a frame strip, the scores, who gets replaced, the one-line joke and the cost for each render option, and let me pick
</swap_gate>

<render>
both options take the real clip and the reference sheet with one prompt: "replace [person described by position and clothing] with the man in the image. keep his exact motion, gestures, mouth movement and timing. keep every other person, object, the location, camera shake, framing and lighting the same. no text."

kling 3.0 omni (cheaper, about $0.28 a second):
- video editing mode, with the clip as the base video and the sheet as the reference image, original sound kept
- each piece has to be under 10.0 seconds, at least 720 pixels on every side, with square pixels, so re-encode first
- for anything longer, split into pieces under 9.5 seconds at calm moments where the person is clearly visible, and render every piece with the exact same sheet and prompt
- compare the last frame of each piece with the first frame of the next, and re-render any piece where the face, hair or outfit jumps
- join the pieces with no audio, then lay the original audio back over the whole thing as one track

seedance 2.5 (premium, about $0.97 a second with a video input):
- up to 30 seconds in one pass with no seams and the best consistency
- editing mode with the clip as the reference video and the sheet as the reference image, then lay the original audio back on

never use kling motion control for this, because it rebuilds the whole scene from its image and rejects crowded clips. never use gemini omni edit mode either, because it blocks any video with a real person in it
</render>

<check>
- make a contact sheet of the finished video and look at every frame
- re-render once if the signature feature morphs, anyone except the target changes, text appears that wasn't there, or hands melt at a key moment
- never do more than 2 render attempts without asking me
</check>

<post>
- caption in my language, deadpan, in character, under 6 words, never explaining the joke
- tag the person replaced and the original creator, because that's how the original artist ends up seeing it
- turn on instagram's ai label for the post and the profile, since unlabelled ai accounts lose reach
- fresh clips go out while the original is still inside its week, and evergreen clips go out at the account's best hour
- first comment from the account is "follow for more" or the catchphrase
- never launch or promote a token, and never imply the original person endorsed the character
</post>

<learn>
- log every post with the lane, scores, render option, cost, and plays at 24 and 72 hours
- the next time you run, scrape the account first and fill those columns in
- after 10 posts, compare plays against each score and each lane, shift the weighting toward whatever actually predicted views, and write down what changed
</learn>

<honesty>
- only put numbers on screen or in captions that you scraped or measured
- mark anything you guessed rather than measured
- if no clip passes the gate today, say so instead of forcing a weak one
</honesty>

<deliverables>
- the final mp4 at the source resolution, with the original audio
- the reference sheet
- a short note on why this clip won and why the runners-up lost
- the caption, tags and posting time
- total spend, and anything a human should still check
</deliverables>

OpenAI shipped an agent update that stops reporting what crashed and starts naming the decision that made the crash possible.

A stack trace points at the line that failed. That line is almost never where the problem was introduced.

> WALK - the failure traced backwards through every call that led into it
> BLAME - the commit that introduced each assumption on that path identified
> ECHO - other places in the codebase running on the same assumption flagged
> RANK - the paths sorted by how much live traffic crosses them

It returns a list of places that have not broken yet, which is a different thing from a list of places that are fine.

A fix without that list is a guess that happened to work. This turns an incident into a map of everything standing on the same floor.
